entrypoints.summary: Incoming W3C baggage HTTP header processed on the baggage propagation extract path of an instrumented HTTP service.

relation_candidates.rationale: The advisory states that attacker-controlled baggage headers can contain arbitrarily many pairs or a large value and that extraction lacks corresponding bounds.
The advisory attributes unbounded CPU and memory consumption from per-pair map allocation to remote denial of service.
The described defect is the absence of item-count and byte-size limits on extraction; the advisory says version 4.8.2 and later resolves the issue, but supplies no implementation diff.
The advisory recommends removing baggage from extraction propagation configuration as a workaround.
The advisory recommends an upstream request-header size cap as a workaround that constrains attacker-supplied baggage-header input before extraction.

impact.affected_asset: Availability and process resources of the instrumented HTTP service.
impact.attacker_capability: Send an oversized or excessively itemized W3C baggage HTTP header to an affected, baggage-enabled HTTP service without authentication.
impact.security_effect: Remote denial of service through unbounded CPU and memory consumption.

causal_trace.summary: A remote unauthenticated actor sends a request with a baggage header containing arbitrarily many comma-separated key-value pairs or one very large value.
Configured baggage maximum-item (default 64) and maximum-byte (default 8192) limits were applied during injection but not while extracting incoming headers, leaving extraction input unbounded.
For each parsed baggage pair, the tracer allocates a hash-map entry on every request; an unbounded extracted header therefore drives unbounded per-request allocation and parsing work.
The resulting unbounded CPU and memory consumption can deny service to an HTTP service with baggage propagation enabled.

failure.operation: Parsing incoming baggage data and allocating one hash-map entry per pair without extract-path item-count or byte-size enforcement.

primary_invariant.statement: Extraction of an incoming W3C baggage header must enforce finite byte-size and item-count bounds before creating per-item baggage-map entries.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The advisory states that the item and byte limits existed only for injection, while the extraction path accepted arbitrarily many pairs or a large value.

quality.review_notes: The OSV/GitHub advisory directly describes the input, extract-path limit omission, per-pair map allocation, impact, scope, and fixed version. No patch commit, source-level extraction routine, regression test, or observed reproduction/run result is present, so exact fixed-code behavior and a test oracle cannot be established from this bundle.

remediation.invariant_restored: Use ddtrace 4.8.2 or later; the advisory identifies that release as resolved. The supplied material does not include a patch diff establishing the exact implementation, while the stated desired safety condition is bounded extraction item count and byte size.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: PyPI ddtrace versions introduced at 0 and fixed at 4.8.2; affected versions are earlier than 4.8.2.
